routes.name: International first-year admission
routes.applicant: Kazakhstan applicant educated outside the destination country
routes.eligibility: Meet university-entrance requirements in your own country and submit strong secondary/leaving results, application documents and one accepted test. Admission to the college precedes declaring a major.
routes.recognition: Kazakhstan diploma equivalence is assessed by Berea; entrance eligibility in the awarding country is required. Do not assume a Grade 11 certificate alone satisfies every document rule.
routes.subjects: General secondary preparation. No programme-specific school-subject minimum verified for this international route.

SAT.detail: SAT 980 is one accepted test; ACT, IELTS, TOEFL or Duolingo may satisfy the published test step instead.

ACT.detail: ACT composite 19; other accepted tests may satisfy the step.

IELTS.detail: IELTS 6 overall and 5 in each area is one alternative.

TOEFL.detail: TOEFL iBT 68 is one published alternative; confirm handling of the revised TOEFL scale.

ENGLISH.detail: At least one approved test is required. SAT/ACT can satisfy that step instead of a separate English test; not an unconditional no-test route.

tuition.note: Gross tuition schedule not captured. All admitted international students receive the separately described funding package; do not treat unknown gross tuition as zero.

routes.mandatoryFees: International FAQ expects a USD 2,200 enrolment deposit, with additional aid possible for students unable to pay. Other upfront travel/visa expenses need checking.
routes.living: Tuition, housing, food and fees are covered by the international package; personal expenses remain. No independent living estimate verified.
routes.nextAction: Check diploma documentation and choose one accepted test before preparing the international application.

awards.name: Aalto University Excellence Scholarship
awards.benefits: Competitive waiver of the full tuition fee. No living-cost package. Programmes can award no scholarships.

awards.application: Select scholarship application on the admission form during the application period; later applications are not accepted.
awards.renewal: Normative study period: three years for the bachelor, full-time study according to approved study plan. Master continuation scholarship has additional conditions and is separate.
awards.upfront: Living expenses, study materials, union/healthcare costs, insurance and travel remain. If no waiver, tuition is normally due as one annual instalment.

awards.name: KAIST Scholarship
awards.benefits: Full tuition for 8 semesters, KRW350000 monthly living allowance and medical insurance. This is maintenance support, not a guarantee that every expense is paid.
awards.eligibility: International Student Admission applicants admitted with scholarship; citizenship and academic admission rules apply.
awards.application: Tick KAIST scholarship in the financial-resources section of the admission form; no separate award application.
awards.renewal: Maintain GPA above 2.7/4.3 after freshman year; confirm terms in offer.
awards.upfront: Application fee, travel, visa, initial housing and living costs may remain; amounts not verified.

awards.renewal: Entry award for first year only; not automatically renewable.
awards.upfront: Tuition can be waived or refunded if already paid; visa, insurance and living costs remain.

awards.name: Waikato Vice-Chancellor’s International Excellence Scholarship
awards.benefits: 2027 regulations: NZD 8000–15000 tuition credit; no living support.
awards.eligibility: New full-time international student, offer of place and at least B+ equivalent. Must not qualify for a country-specific version; current Waikato/College students, sponsored and exchange routes are excluded.
awards.application: Apply after receiving an offer, before paying tuition or applying for a visa. Offshore A-trimester applicants must apply before 30 November; B-trimester before 31 May. Confirm the year and cutoff.

awards.upfront: Do not pay tuition or apply for a visa before the scholarship application; remaining tuition, insurance, travel and living costs need funding.
